why: A count is not a comparison. These are the SORTED FAILURE IDENTITIES of each full-suite run, so a later reader can diff them instead of trusting a number, and so the matched pair survives the container that produced it.
how_each_run_was_made: a frozen `git archive <sha> | tar -x` checkout, its own freshly migrated database, `python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:randomly`
the_matched_pair: 60de482 against 6d75275, minutes apart on the same machine: 178 and 178, and the identity sets are IDENTICAL -- nothing new, nothing gone, nothing newly passing.
not_a_clean_gate: 178 pre-existing failures remain on the baseline itself. Nothing here claims otherwise.
